Sounds like a plan. A bit more overhead to our tiny VPS but I see no other alternative if we want to keep everything in house).

On the other hand, as an alternative to avoid the double counting you could simply track if a user visited/clicked a link using his/her username, not the IP. In that case you don't need to worry about storing IPs, hashing it, etc.

This will of course not count people who are not logged on. So that is the downside. In that case the counter would simply show how many registered and logged users have clicked on a post (which is a good indicator too).

That could be another interesting metric (nice to have) although it wouldn't have much relevance since most people who come here are lurkers and don't log in unless they want to submit something or vote. I'll prioritize the total views for now but the views by logged-in users should also be developed at some point.

This is now implemented. A pretty basic implementation but I think it will do for now.

Here is how it works:

  • a user views a submission for the first time
  • the system gets the users IP, encrypts it using SHA512 and stores the encrypted IP in the database along with the submission ID that the user viewed
  • the view counter for given post is incremented by 1
